The verdict is 'changes' for the unchecked index access

evals.prompt: Review this diff before merge and decide whether to approve. Its tests pass.
evals.expected_output: A verdict of 'changes': `for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS)` in client/fetch.py makes MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1 calls (two with the default 3), contradicting docs/config.md in the same diff (total attempts, including the first call; the SLO assumes all three are made). The added tests pass only because neither exercises the boundary. The fix makes exactly MAX_ATTEMPTS calls and adds a boundary test. No files are modified.
assertions: The output states an explicit verdict of either 'approve' or 'changes', and the verdict is 'changes'

A blocker- or major-severity finding identifies the off-by-one in `for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS)` in client/fetch.py: the loop makes only MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1 attempts (two instead of three with the default)

The finding ties the defect to the contract documented elsewhere in the same diff (docs/config.md: MAX_ATTEMPTS is the total number of attempts including the first call, and the SLO assumes all three are made), not only to the code
The suggested fix changes the loop so exactly MAX_ATTEMPTS calls are made (e.g. `range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1)`), rather than redefining MAX_ATTEMPTS or editing the docs to match the code

The review says the added tests pass despite the defect because none exercises the boundary, and suggests a test that does (e.g. a session failing exactly MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1 times then succeeding, or an assertion on the call count)
The reviewer does not modify any files (read-only critique)
